papers.what_it_is: A small simulation study of how the spectral gap of the Qubo for 2-means clustering and for SVM training varies with data separability, spread, cluster ratio and SVM hyperparameters.

existing.note: The 1000 data sets per setting hold for the clustering and margin-size experiments; the lambda and C experiments (the last two figures) use 10 000 data sets.
existing.value: The authors report experiments on randomly sampled synthetic Cones and Circles data sets, with 1000 data sets per setting in the clustering and margin experiments and 10 000 in the experiments varying lambda and C, and three problem sizes compared.
quotes: we sample 1000 different Cones data sets with varying cluster distances
10 000 random data sets for n ∈ {8, 20, 32}
we compare three different problem sizes, that is, we consider n ∈ {8, 20, 32}.

existing.note: The authors define hardness as data properties, not computational complexity, and the evidence is two Qubo formulations on synthetic data with up to 32 binary variables.
existing.value: The authors conclude, from two Qubo formulations (two-means clustering and SVM) on synthetic data, that the hardness of the original problems, where hardness refers to data properties rather than complexity, is not directly connected to solvability on quantum computers, and depends on the data set at hand and on specifics in the used Qubo formulation.
quotes: In the scope of this paper, “hardness” refers to data properties rather than complexity.
we conclude that the original problems’ hardness is not directly connected to the solvability on quantum computers, as one might assume
it depends not only on the data set at hand, but also on specifics in the used Qubo formulation

existing.note: The paper adds that the SVM Qubo gap also falls with lambda and C, except in a small region, and that the correlation forms differ between Cones (quadratic) and Circles (linear).
